initial_failures: TypeScript TS2322 in storage.onChanged: dynamic property value was unknown. Fixed by narrowing a local variable; complete extension test/build rerun passed.

First desktop acceptance attempts were blocked by the core-tests firewall permission dialog, confirmed by screenshot. User canceled it. Remote input to relaunch tests was unreliable; a fresh Sandbox directly ran the remaining desktop scripts. No firewall setting was changed.
limits: Three alternating rounds in one Windows Sandbox, not a cross-hardware guarantee.
Core benchmark covers 1000 IPC progress commits after event-ring warmup, not desktop frame latency or Internet throughput.
No real cloud provider, physical casting/TVBox, multi-hour soak, new MSI installation, signing, GitHub push or release.
Candidate remains local and uncommitted; previous reports still apply only to their recorded hashes.

performance_follow_up.control: baseline-a and baseline-b use the same executable; order rotates across three rounds
performance_follow_up.fixture: 1000 paused tasks; 4100 warmup commands; 1000 progress commits; changing bytes versus one task with 500 persisted logs and repeated log text
performance_follow_up.invariants: All task states and final bytes verified; all persisted repeated-progress log row values unchanged, including IDs and timestamps.
performance_follow_up.conclusion: Repeated-full-log workload uses less Core CPU in this sample. Changing-progress candidate P95 remains higher; identical-baseline controls also fluctuate. Overall speedup and cause of the P95 difference remain unproven. Retain the bounded no-insert/no-trim change without claiming a general latency improvement.
limits: Prior backend and candidate binaries, not a freshly rebuilt single-variable A/B experiment.
Three rounds per case in one Sandbox; no cross-hardware or multi-hour guarantee.
No host product run/install, cloud calls, signing, commit, push, release or MSI build.
